product_overview: RUNIX is a browser-based cloud development platform that lets developers create or import projects, edit code, run commands, preview applications, and manage Git workflows from the browser. It separates the control plane from isolated execution runtimes so user code never runs on the API host.
core_goals: Provide authenticated developer accounts with secure session management
Enable project creation, listing, and workspace management from the dashboard
Support template-based project creation for React, Node.js, Python FastAPI, MERN, and blank Docker environments
Allow safe workspace file browsing, reading, writing, creation, deletion, and renaming within project boundaries
Run user commands in isolated runtimes with resource limits, terminal access, and live preview support
Expose basic Git operations and GitHub repository import workflows
Deliver a Stitch-faithful frontend experience for the landing page, dashboard, workspace, and IDE
Provide real observability, structured error handling, and security protections across the platform

features.name: Authentication API
features.description: Developer registration, login, logout, current-user lookup, and session management for secure access to RUNIX.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/auth/register with email, password, and display_name -> Receive 200 with created user -> POST /api/v1/auth/login with valid credentials -> Receive 200 with JWT/session token -> GET /api/v1/auth/me with token -> Receive 200 with authenticated user summary -> POST /api/v1/auth/logout with token -> Receive 200 logout success

POST /api/v1/auth/register with an email that already exists -> Receive 409 Email already exists -> POST /api/v1/auth/login with invalid password -> Receive 401 Invalid credentials -> GET /api/v1/auth/me without auth -> Receive 401 Unauthorized

features.name: Project Management API
features.description: Create, list, retrieve, update, and delete developer projects owned by authenticated users.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/projects with name, template, and visibility while authenticated -> Receive 201 with project details -> GET /api/v1/projects -> Receive 200 with project list -> GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id} -> Receive 200 with project details

POST /api/v1/projects without authentication -> Receive 401 Unauthorized -> GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id} for a project not owned by the user -> Receive 403 Project access denied or 404 Project not found -> GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id} for a missing project -> Receive 404 Project not found

features.name: Templates Catalog API
features.description: Expose the supported starter templates used when creating new projects.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/templates -> Receive 200 with template list including react-vite-ts, node-typescript, python-fastapi, mern, and blank-docker -> Select a template in the project creation flow -> POST /api/v1/projects with that template -> Receive 201 with created project
GET /api/v1/templates -> Receive 200 template list -> Submit POST /api/v1/projects with an unsupported template identifier -> Receive 422 or 400 template validation error

features.name: Workspace Filesystem API
features.description: Safely list, read, create, update, rename, and delete files and directories inside a project workspace.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/files -> Receive 200 with file tree -> GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/files/content?path=src/App.tsx -> Receive 200 with file content -> PUT /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/files/content with path and content -> Receive 200 write success

GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/files/content?path=../secret.txt -> Receive 400 or 403 path validation error -> PUT /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/files/content with absolute or traversal path -> Receive 400 invalid path -> GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/files/content for missing file -> Receive 404 File not found

features.name: Runtime Lifecycle API
features.description: Create, start, stop, restart, and inspect isolated project runtimes with persistent metadata and resource limits.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/runtime/start -> Receive 202 Accepted with starting status -> GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/runtime -> Receive 200 with running runtime metadata -> POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/runtime/stop -> Receive 202 Accepted with stopping status

POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/runtime/start without authorization -> Receive 401 or 403 -> POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/runtime/start while runtime is already starting -> Receive 409 runtime state conflict -> GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/runtime for missing project -> Receive 404 Project not found

features.name: Terminal WebSocket
features.description: Provide an authenticated interactive terminal session over WebSocket connected to the project runtime.
user_flows: Open WebSocket /ws/projects/{project_id}/terminal with authenticated session -> Receive connected message with terminal_session_id and runtime_id -> Send input message with shell command -> Receive output messages from the runtime PTY -> Send resize message -> Receive resized terminal behavior

Open WebSocket /ws/projects/{project_id}/terminal without authentication -> Receive 401 or connection close -> Send malformed WebSocket message -> Receive error code WEBSOCKET_MESSAGE_INVALID -> Connect when runtime is unavailable -> Receive RUNTIME_NOT_AVAILABLE or runtime_status failed

features.name: Command Execution API
features.description: Execute non-interactive commands inside the isolated runtime and track execution status and results.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/commands with command and timeout_seconds -> Receive 202 Accepted with execution_id -> GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/commands/{execution_id} -> Receive completed status and exit code -> Inspect command output in runtime/terminal tooling

POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/commands without a running runtime -> Receive 409 or 503 runtime unavailable -> POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/commands with invalid or disallowed command -> Receive 422 or policy rejection -> GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/commands/{execution_id} for missing execution -> Receive 404 not found

features.name: Git Operations API
features.description: Support local Git status, diff, staging, unstaging, commit, push, pull, branch listing, and branch checkout for project workspaces.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/git/status -> Receive 200 with branch, staged, modified, and untracked files -> POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/git/commit with message -> Receive 200 with commit_sha -> GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/git/branches -> Receive 200 with branch list

POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/git/checkout with invalid branch -> Receive 422 branch validation error -> POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/git/push without permitted credentials or permission -> Receive 401/403 or queued job with later failure -> Pull or checkout with uncommitted changes that would be overwritten -> Receive 409 conflict and preserve local changes

features.name: GitHub Integration API
features.description: Authenticate with GitHub, list accessible repositories, and import repositories into RUNIX projects asynchronously.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/github/install -> Begin GitHub authorization flow -> GET /api/v1/github/repositories -> Receive 200 with repository list -> POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/github/import with repository_id and branch -> Receive 202 with job_id

POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/github/import without GitHub authorization -> Receive 403 GitHub access denied -> GET /api/v1/github/repositories with expired or invalid session -> Receive 401 or 403 -> GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id} for import progress -> Receive queued, running, completed, or failed status

features.name: Health Check API
features.description: Expose lightweight system health and readiness endpoints for monitoring and deployment validation.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/health -> Receive 200 with ok status -> GET /api/v1/health/ready -> Receive 200 ready when dependencies are healthy -> Use response in deployment smoke checks
GET /api/v1/health/ready when PostgreSQL or Redis is unavailable -> Receive 503 Service Unavailable -> Monitor failure through observability tooling
